newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stocks close higher, led by blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stocks close higher, led by blue-chips.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended its two-hour session on Thursday higher, boosted by blue-chip companies, including conglomerate ONA Group, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 437.15 points, up 0.30 percent compared with Wednesday's session.
"The ONA's and Wafabank surge was the engine behind the bourse index rise for the second consecutive day," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate which has diversified stakes in 100 companies, jumped 10 dirhams to close at 495 dirhams after reporting improved profits, he said.
ONA showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to 328.6 million dirhams in the first half of the year, from 272.4 million a year earlier.
ONA and its subsidiaries control between 65 and 80 percent of Morocco's edible oil, sugar and milk market, stockbrokers said.

The conglomerate's listed subsidiaries, sugar refinery Cosumar, agro-industry Centrale Laitiere, edible oil firm Lesieur and Financiere Diwan, all posted positive results in the first half of the year compared with a year earlier, the group said.
Wafabank, one of the country's largest banks, rose 15 dirhams to close at 520 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 14.5 million dirhams compared with 20.5 million on Wednesday.
